place: Brazil, Indonesia, Democratic Republic of the Congo
data: forest loss data, product not named
method: Emerging Hot Spot Analysis in ArcGIS with big data analytical tools
finding: Brazilian loss declined but shifted to the cerrado, loss intensified in Riau and Kalimantan, and new hot spots emerged across the Democratic Republic of the Congo near Beni and Kisangani.
gap_quote: As sources of data for global forest monitoring grow larger, more complex and numerous, data analysis and interpretation become critical bottlenecks for effectively using them to inform land use policy discussions.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Okapi Wildlife Reserve
data: Joint Research Centre Tropical Moist Forest annual maps at 30 m
method: Trajectory Analysis and DynamicPATCH, with change split into Quantity, Exchange and Alternation components
predictors: study zone of agriculture, mining or hunting-conservation
finding: Agriculture zone change mostly alternated but moved toward persistent non-forest after 2022, mining expanded persistently with Quantity at 98 per cent of change, and the hunting-conservation zone stayed largely stable.
gap_quote: Tropical protected areas face pressures from smallholder agriculture and illegal mining, yet many monitoring approaches reduce these dynamics to net forest loss, obscuring whether change is alternating or persistent.

place: Gabon, hilly region of central Gabon
data: TanDEM-X InSAR phase height, aboveground biomass change in four selectively logged plots
method: relationship of TanDEM-X InSAR phase height to aboveground biomass change, with reduced multilooking and pass direction chosen pixel by pixel
finding: TanDEM-X phase height tracked aboveground biomass change in four logged plots in hilly central Gabon, and less multilooking and pass direction chosen per pixel improved degradation estimates on steep slopes.
gap_quote: Current satellite remote sensing methods struggle to detect and map forest degradation, which is a critical issue as it is likely a major and growing source of carbon emissions and biodiveristy loss.

data: Landsat 7 ETM 2000 and Landsat 8 OLI 2014 images, topographic maps
method: Landsat land use and land cover change analysis, 250 household surveys in 13 villages, 11 focus group discussions
predictors: household cultivation of food and cash crops, dependence on timber and non-timber forest products
finding: From 2000 to 2014, dense forest dropped to 90.2 per cent, settlements grew from 744.6 to 2148.8 hectares and farmland from 9400.4 to 11117.16 hectares.
gap_quote: But the recent expansion of human activities around Cameroon’s Rumpi Hills Forest Reserve in this Era of Sustainable Development Goals is a call for concern.

area: 1,247,500 ha under collective contracts and 165,700 ha under individual contracts
data: not stated
method: impact evaluation by matching, with sensitivity analysis for hidden bias
predictors: Socio Bosque Program payment, individual or collective contract, observable covariates not named
finding: Socio Bosque Program reduced deforestation by 1.5 per cent in paid forests, by 3.4 and about 1 per cent under individual and collective contracts, and conventional estimates overstated avoided deforestation.
gap_quote: Conventional estimates of the impact of the SBP tend to overestimate avoided deforestation because they do not control for observable covariates that correlate with or affect both SBP participation and deforestation.

place: Republic of the Congo, selective logging concession in the north
data: SPOT4Take5 and RapidEye time series
method: time series analysis of fine resolution imagery
finding: Most logging gaps disappeared within a few months, showing very rapid forest cover change after selective logging.

data: not stated
method: two econometric models of demand for logging, fuelwood and conversion to agricultural land, with scenario projections
predictors: population density, price of wood, distance from Bangkok, rice yields, price of upland crops relative to rice, income, price of kerosene, rural road density, irrigation infrastructure
finding: All variables except irrigation infrastructure contributed significantly to deforestation, led by population density, and scenario projections showed no single policy could reverse deforestation.
gap_quote: The researchers made several projections using different scenarios and learned that no one implemented policy can reverse deforestation.

data: satellite-based maps of annual forest loss, product not named
method: projection of tropical deforestation under alternative policy scenarios, marginal abatement cost curves
predictors: topography, accessibility, protected status, potential agricultural revenue, forest cover
finding: Without new policies 289 million hectares would be cleared from 2016 to 2050, releasing 169 GtCO2, and a carbon price of 20 US dollars per tonne would avoid 41 GtCO2.
gap_quote: Yet previous efforts to project the cost-effectiveness of policies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from future deforestation across the tropics were hampered by crude available data on historical forest loss.

data: forest loss data, product not named
method: comparison of forest loss with satellite, station-based and reanalysis precipitation across spatial scales
finding: Forest loss reduced precipitation at scales above 50 km, most at 200 km, and future Congo deforestation would reduce local precipitation 8 to 10 per cent in 2100.
gap_quote: Previous work has assessed the impacts of tropical deforestation on precipitation, but these efforts have been largely limited to case studies2.

data: not stated
method: synthetic control method
predictors: local initiative, deforestation before the intervention
validation: fit of the synthetic control to Paragominas before the intervention
finding: The synthetic control matched Paragominas before 2008, and the local initiative lowered deforestation significantly below the synthetic control in 2012.
gap_quote: These methods generally require large samples for statistical comparisons, presenting a challenge for evaluating innovative policies implemented within a few pioneering jurisdictions.

data: not stated
method: business as usual and avoided deforestation scenarios for district and provincial jurisdictions
finding: Stopping oil palm concession deforestation could cut emissions up to 15 per cent below business as usual, and ending production forest deforestation would avoid about 21 per cent.
gap_quote: Jurisdictional approaches to REDD+ have received less attention than project-based REDD+ activities, yet they are needed for the successful implementation of REDD+ at the national level.

data: not stated
method: Bayesian state-space synthetic control model joining ex-ante baseline projection with ex-post dynamic baseline updating
validation: ex-ante baseline compared with the ex-post baseline
measures: ex-post baseline inside the 90 per cent predictive interval of the ex-ante baseline
finding: Applied to a Brazilian REDD+ project, the model found a small positive effect but over-crediting, and the ex-ante baseline 90 per cent predictive interval contained the ex-post baseline.
gap_quote: Carbon credits from the reducing emissions from deforestation and degradation (REDD+) projects have been criticized for issuing junk carbon credits due to invalid ex-ante baselines.

data: not stated
method: mosquito night catches on human bait over one year in two hamlets, one beside the airport and one 3 km away
finding: Anopheles moucheti formed 95 per cent of vectors, deforestation favoured Anopheles gambiae, and transmission was 106 infective bites per person per year near the airport against 68 farther away.

data: panel dataset of forest cover, product not named
method: matched triple difference
predictors: moratorium area, dryland or peatland forest
finding: Dryland forest inside moratorium areas kept at most 0.65 per cent more cover, peatland forest was unaffected, and emissions reductions reached 67.8 to 86.9 million tons from 2011 to 2018.
gap_quote: By contrast, carbon-rich peatland forest was unaffected by the moratorium.

data: permanent sample plot data from intact and logged-over forest
method: error partition of emission factors from four equally likely allometric models, an uncertainty analysis
finding: Allometric model choice gave the largest error in the biomass difference between intact and logged forest, 40 per cent of the sum of squares, and weighting models could reduce it.
gap_quote: Using data from permanent sample plots in a tropical moist forest in central Africa and considering four allometric models with equal likelihood, the largest source of error in the estimate of the difference of biomass between intact and logged-over forest was that due to the model choice (40 % of the sum of squares).

data: multi-temporal Landsat imagery for 1994, 2009 and 2024
method: supervised classification of Landsat imagery with ground control points, change detection
finding: From 1994 to 2024, dense forest declined sharply as cropland rose from 3.06 to 30.42 per cent and built-up area from 1.42 to 9.11 per cent.
gap_quote: These dynamics pose significant challenges to environmental sustainability and effective land governance, underscoring the urgent need for comprehensive land use planning and management interventions.

data: not stated
method: weighted multi-criteria analysis of three historical baseline methods and one dynamic model baseline
finding: Each baseline method had strengths and weaknesses, and the dynamic model performed best environmentally but its data and capacity demands limited its use in many developing countries.
gap_quote: Although the dynamic model allows for the best environmental and for comparatively good economic performance, its high demand for data and technical capacity limit the current applicability in many developing countries.

data: NASA Global Land Survey Landsat imagery, gaps filled from United States Geological Survey and other Landsat archives and SPOT
method: systematic sample at degree confluence points, visual screening of image pairs and gap filling
finding: The sample reached 3945 image pairs for 1990 and 2000, 98 per cent of targets, with missing pairs concentrated in the Congo Basin, where about 15 per cent stayed unsampled.
gap_quote: No suitable image pairs were found for 71 confluence points, which were not randomly distributed, but mostly concentrated in the Congo basin, where around 15% of the region remains un-sampled.

data: observed deforestation, product not named, five biomass density maps
method: artificial neural network, nine state-specific calibrated models spatializing the plan baseline
finding: Forest loss in 2006 to 2017 was 62,321 square kilometres below the baseline, avoiding 1.5 plus or minus 0.4 Pg CO2, 93 per cent in Mato Grosso and Rondônia.
gap_quote: Alarming rates of forest loss in the Amazon region gained international attention in the past, but deforestation declined substantially since 2004 (although the rate has trended upwards since 2012).

data: field plots of forest, pasture, oil palm and secondary forest
method: radiocarbon and stable carbon isotope analysis of soil organic matter across land uses
finding: Carbon stocks fell sharply under pasture and oil palm, pasture soils lost young carbon preferentially, and oil palm soils may retain enough new carbon to offset initial losses.
gap_quote: However, rapid deforestation threatens the stability of this carbon.

area: harvesting areas of over 22,000 ha, UAV survey of about 1500 ha
data: Sentinel-1 SAR time series, monthly harvesting areas, over 6000 harvested tree locations, UAV canopy gap dataset
method: two-step two-scale Sentinel-1 change detection, textural indices at 300 m then canopy gap detection at 10 m from monthly differences
validation: independent UAV canopy gap dataset and harvest records, compared with other available approaches
measures: omission and commission errors 0.05 or less for harvesting areas, global accuracy 0.89 for canopy gaps, gap omission 0.39 and commission 0.05
finding: Harvesting areas were mapped with errors of 0.05 or less and canopy gaps at 0.89 accuracy, including most small gaps, while other approaches missed at least 70 per cent.
gap_quote: Forest degradation is a major threat to tropical forests, and effective monitoring using remotely sensed data is subject to significant challenges.

place: Cameroon, Kedjom Keku forest, northwest Cameroon
data: remote sensing images for 1986, 2003 and 2018, sensor not named
method: remote sensing and GIS land cover change analysis with seven classes, semi-structured questionnaires, five vegetation plots
predictors: reported infrastructure, over-grazing, farmland expansion, land rights, land tenure, equitability, soil fertility
finding: Built-up area rose from 0.63 per cent in 2003 to 20.46 per cent in 2018, and infrastructure, over-grazing and farmland expansion were the main reported direct causes of degradation.
gap_quote: Conservation of tropical rainforest is an important aspect of climate change mitigation, and baseline information through inventories of forests is paramount so as to enable the putting in place of proper management strategies.

data: not stated
method: participatory scenario development of business as usual and green economy scenarios, with impacts on carbon, biodiversity and water yield
finding: Business as usual change would cause 296 million tonnes of carbon stock loss by 2025, against 133 million under a green economy, and reduce habitat for endemic and rare species.
gap_quote: Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation plus the conservation of forest carbon stocks, sustainable management of forests and enhancement of forest carbon stocks in developing countries (REDD+) requires information on land-use and land-cover changes (LULCCs) and carbon emission trends from the past to the present and into the future.

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Methods must suit the research question, and land cover change models need better integration of social science knowledge and a comprehensive theory of land use change.
gap_quote: Quantitative data on where, when and why land-cover changes take place globally are still incomplete.

place: Congo Basin, a typical export-oriented forest concession
data: not stated
method: Monte Carlo simulation of logging intensity reduction scenarios, break-even prices of permanent carbon credits
finding: Reducing logging intensity was attractive with complete cessation of logging or in little exploited, low-profit forests, and carbon prices were too low to change logging practices.
gap_quote: Carbon market prices are too low to be an incentive to change logging practices toward more climate-smart forest management, and a change of paradigm to change actors' behaviors would be needed.

data: official land use and cover change statistics
method: ex-ante assessment of REDD opportunity costs for projected deforestation
finding: At least 1 million hectares of projected deforestation in Mato Grosso and Amazonas could be compensated at current carbon prices until 2017, at 330 million to over 1 billion dollars.

place: Brazil, Mato Grosso, Central Africa, Kenya and Tanzania border
data: remote sensing maps of land cover change and active fires
method: landscape-scale spatial association analysis of active fire maps and land cover change maps
finding: Fire impacts on land cover varied and were mainly controlled by land use, and fires were significantly associated with forest cover change but not shown to mark deforestation hot spots.
gap_quote: There is thus a need to consider the socioeconomic purpose of biomass burning and the context in which such activities are undertaken.

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: The Congo Basin may become the next oil palm frontier, company certification is unlikely to curb deforestation, and a regional strategy including smallholders and informal markets is needed.
gap_quote: As agricultural land becomes increasingly scarce in Southeast Asia, and regulatory pressures continue to intensify, the Congo Basin could become the next frontier for oil palm expansion.

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Setting the reference level at 0.275 per cent a year, far above the historical 0.02 per cent, all but guaranteed Guyana's success, and Norway paid in full despite breaches.
gap_quote: It argues that the establishment of, and continual negotiations around, the reference level rate illustrate how the Guyana-Norway REDD+ agreement was always more about ensuring the programme’s ‘success’ than materially reducing deforestation in Guyana.

data: forest cover data of six ex post evaluations, products not named
method: synthesis of six independent ex post evaluations covering 44 REDD+ projects
finding: Most of 44 REDD+ projects reduced deforestation but claimed 10.7 times the justified avoided deforestation, driven by selection bias in control areas and modelling, not forest cover data.
gap_quote: Independent evaluations have shown substantial over-issuance of REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation) credits traded on the voluntary carbon market.

place: Togo, Benin, Nigeria, Cameroon, seven forests
data: forest structural complexity measurements
method: survey of 1956 respondents with semi-structured questionnaires for 328 forest users, integrated with forest pressure data and structural complexity measures
predictors: spatially explicit demographic and governance pressure on forests, reported forest uses
finding: Logging, fire and agriculture were seen as driving degradation, high socio-economic pressure matched higher measured degradation, and the most pressured community was least concerned about degradation.
gap_quote: Tropical forests face fragmentation, degradation, and conversion, leading to biodiversity loss, reduced carbon storage, and diminished ecosystem services.

data: not stated
method: assessment framework scoring the relevance, magnitude and likelihood of imminent development changes for forest conservation
predictors: development agenda components including agriculture, transport, urban and energy infrastructure, poverty reduction, tourism, industry, education, governance
finding: Across much of the tropics, risks to forests from agriculture, transport and urban infrastructure could worsen and new energy infrastructure risks could emerge, while enabling conditions still need much improvement.
gap_quote: Exploring this topic requires knowledge of which areas of the development agenda are likely to show the greatest progress, and how these expected changes relate to the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation that are currently affecting forests, or which may emerge as result of development-related changes.

data: low and high spatial resolution satellite data, products not named
method: probability-based sampling combining low and high spatial resolution satellite data
finding: Clearing from 2000 to 2005 was 1.39 per cent of the humid tropical biome, 27.2 million hectares, with Brazil 47.8 per cent and Africa 5.4 per cent of it.
gap_quote: Despite incremental improvements in our ability to quantify rates of forest clearing, there is still no definitive understanding on global trends.

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Setting national baselines is among the most troublesome REDD issues, and expectations of payments are unrealistically high, which may hinder agreement and raise the risk of hot air.
gap_quote: One of the most troublesome issues concerns setting national baselines (= emission quotas).

data: not stated
method: spatial analysis of oil palm expansion against forest cover and the locations of informal and company-owned mills
predictors: proximity to informal mills and company-owned mills, agro-industrial concessions
finding: From 2000 to 2015, 67 per cent of oil palm expansion in Southwest Cameroon replaced forest, mostly outside agro-industrial concessions and near informal mills rather than company mills.
gap_quote: Despite accounting for 24% (4.5 Mha) of the world's total oil palm cultivated area, expansion dynamics in sub-Saharan Africa have been overlooked.

data: observed deforestation in control sites, product not named
method: synthetic control methods for causal inference, comparing project baselines with ex-post counterfactuals
finding: Most of 27 conservation projects in six countries did not reduce deforestation, and where projects did, reductions were substantially lower than claimed against their ex-ante baselines.
gap_quote: Our findings show that most projects have not reduced deforestation.

data: not stated
method: study of the transnational advocacy network, spatial analysis of areas made available by a doubled High Carbon Stock threshold
finding: Zero Deforestation commitments strongly shaped oil palm development in Gabon and Cameroon, and the thesis showed areas a doubled High Carbon Stock threshold would open to plantations.
gap_quote: In the past five years, much concern has been expressed about the fast expansion of large plantations of oil palm in tropical forest in African countries.

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Debate has neglected how REDD+ benefits reaching countries will change local land use behaviour, and frameworks and models of interacting land use factors are needed to assess subnational impacts.
gap_quote: However, while there has been much discussion on global institutional architectures required to channel international finance streams to individual countries, what has been largely missing from the debate so far has been how these benefits reaching the national level will be used to encourage change in behaviors at the local level.

data: GIMMS NDVI time series, 16 published studies
method: review of 16 studies, dry-season NDVI trend analysis separating tree and grass signals
finding: Dry-season NDVI rose significantly on 4.0 per cent and fell on 3.52 per cent of non-rainforest woody vegetation from 1982 to 2006, with increases north of the Congo Basin.
gap_quote: We hypothesize that areas of increasing dry-season NDVI are undergoing woody encroachment, but the coarse resolution of the study and uncertain relationship between NDVI and woody cover mean that the results should be interpreted with caution; certainly, these results do not contradict studies finding widespread deforestation throughout the continent.

place: Indonesia, Brandan Barat Subdistrict, Langkat Regency, North Sumatra
data: Landsat imagery at 30 m
method: CA-Markov spatial simulation with multitemporal Landsat land use change analysis
validation: Kappa accuracy assessment, reference data not stated
finding: Mangrove area fell from 2,282.49 hectares in 2004 to 1,292.67 hectares in 2014 and rose to 1,367.01 hectares in 2024, while plantations grew from 2,792.88 to 3,775.50 hectares.
gap_quote: These conditions increase pressure on protected zones and potentially reduce environmental carrying capacity.

data: ENVISAT ASAR and ALOS PALSAR backscatter
method: supervised analysis of SAR backscatter wavelet frame statistics, wavelet variance scaling signatures fitted by a third-degree polynomial
finding: Wavelet scaling signatures of C-band ENVISAT ASAR significantly separated intact from degraded forest, while ALOS PALSAR results were not significant.
gap_quote: Forest degradation is an important issue in global environmental studies, albeit not yet well defined in quantitative terms.

data: chronosequence plots of cropland and fallow forest aged 4 to 7, 20 to 30 and over 50 years
method: soil organic carbon stock and natural 13C abundance by soil layer to 100 cm across a fallow chronosequence
finding: Soil organic carbon peaked at 136.6 Mg C per hectare in 4 to 7 year fallow and fell to 106.4 in mature forest as the C4 grass contribution declined.
gap_quote: Soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics after slash-burn agriculture are poorly understood in African tropical forest, though recent studies have revealed C4 grass invasion as a forest understory influences SOC dynamics after deforestation.

data: not stated
method: three economic models of global land use and management
finding: Avoided deforestation was a competitive low-cost abatement option, and a 10 per cent cut would save 0.3 to 0.6 Gt CO2 annually at 0.4 to 1.7 billion dollars a year.
gap_quote: United Nations Framework Convention for Climate Change talks are now considering mechanisms for avoiding deforestation (AD), but the economic potential of AD has yet to be addressed.

data: not stated
method: review of 377 REDD+ projects from the International Database on REDD+ Projects, comparison of 86 projects' accounting parameters with national carbon accounting
finding: Projects claimed 3.67 tCO2e per hectare a year, needed over 40-fold upscaling, and 63 of 86 in Colombia, Indonesia and Peru used a parameter differing from national accounting.
gap_quote: This figure - combined with projects limited coverage - implies that projects need to be upscaled more than 40x to fulfil the potential contribution of tropical and subtropical forests towards limiting global warming to well below 2oC.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, remote area of the Congo Basin rainforest
data: plot-level land conversion data, remote sensing data, product not named
method: randomized control trial of modern seed promotion
finding: Promoting modern seeds did not raise overall deforestation by small farmers, but they cleared more primary and less secondary forest, which the authors linked to nitrogen demand.
gap_quote: However, the effect of related land use changes on deforestation and biodiversity is ambiguous.

data: observed deforestation, product not named
method: econometric model of the deforestation response to carbon payments, calibrated on observed deforestation, simulating incentive structures
predictors: carbon payments, spatial variation in benefits and costs of converting land to agriculture
finding: Emissions would have fallen 20 to 31 per cent under mandatory incentives, 17 to 26 per cent under improved voluntary ones and 6 to 9 per cent under basic ones.
gap_quote: In contrast, a "basic voluntary incentive structure" modeled after a standard payment-for-environmental-services program would have reduced emissions nationally by only 45-76 MtCO(2)e/y (6-9%), while generating a programmatic budget shortfall.

data: Landsat Photosynthetic Vegetation fractions, ALOS PALSAR and Sentinel-1B SAR, deforestation reference data
method: PVts-β non-seasonal change detection on Landsat fractions, and five machine learning classifiers on Landsat and SAR fused by principal component analysis
validation: deforestation reference data, classifiers calibrated with cross-validation and Monte Carlo cross-validation
measures: overall accuracy 92.91 per cent for the time series map and 91.82 per cent for the best classifier
finding: The time series change map reached 92.91 per cent overall accuracy and the best machine learning classification 91.82 per cent, mapping forest, cropland, bare soil and water.

data: national land use and cover data for 1993, product not named
method: land use cover change modelling under business as usual and pessimistic socioeconomic and climate scenarios for three periods, hotspot identification
predictors: distance from roads, distance from human settlements, slope, aridity, evapotranspiration
finding: By 2050, grassland and tropical evergreen forest would lose 20 to 33 per cent under business as usual or 43 to 46 per cent under a pessimistic scenario.
gap_quote: Modelling suggests that by 2050 grassland and tropical evergreen forest will be the most endangered ecosystems, having lost 20-33% (BAU) or 43-46% (pessimistic scenario) of their extent in comparison to 1993.
